(you may click CTRL+C to copy full instructions)

Make sure virtualization is enabled in BIOS.

Open PowerShell as Administrator and run:

dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux /all /norestart

dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:VirtualMachinePlatform /all /norestart

wsl --install

Install Devin inside WSL:

wsl

curl -fsSL https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash

Start devin to login:

devin

When a Visual Studio build finishes with errors, automatically send the errors (and warnings, for context) to the active code agent so it can fix them. Only sends when an agent terminal is running and the build actually has errors.
When clipboard text is short it is inserted into the prompt directly. When it exceeds the truncation threshold it is saved to a temp file and attached, avoiding paste truncation.
When enabled, "Send Selection" only inserts the file path and line numbers (e.g. "File: foo.cs (lines 10-15)"), without the selected code. The AI agent reads the file directly.
When enabled, Claude Code starts every session in plan mode, Restart included. Takes effect on the next start.
When enabled, Claude Code starts with --dangerously-skip-permissions
When enabled, Codex starts with --ask-for-approval never
When enabled, Cursor Agent starts with --yolo to skip all approvals
When enabled, Devin starts with --permission-mode dangerous
When enabled, Grok starts with --always-approve to approve every action automatically
When enabled, Qwen Code starts with --yolo to approve every action automatically
When enabled, Run and Run without debugging clean the solution before launching.
When enabled, Run and Run without debugging rebuild the solution before launching. If the rebuild fails, launching is skipped.
When enabled, prompts above ~1 KB are saved to a temp file and only the file path is sent. Avoids paste truncation of large content.
When enabled, script windows close automatically after the script exits. When disabled, they stay open so you can read the output.
When enabled, the action appears as a button on the notification and runs only when you click it. When disabled, the action runs automatically. Recommended on for scripts, run, and rebuild.

When enabled, the clipboard is never used to send a prompt. The prompt is saved to a temp file and only a short file reference is typed into the terminal via simulated keystrokes. Use this if another app (clipboard manager, Remote Desktop, security tool) holds the clipboard and breaks normal paste-based sending.

Available only with the Command Prompt terminal type — Windows Terminal does not accept the simulated keystrokes this uses.

When enabled, the panel shows the conversation with the agent as a chat, driven by the agent's own structured protocol instead of a console window. Answers stream in, tool calls and their results are shown as collapsible cards, and token usage and cost are reported for each turn.

Agents without a structured channel keep using the embedded terminal automatically. The terminal settings below apply only when the terminal is in use.

When enabled, the prompt box shows the last prompt you sent, dimmed, until you start typing — so you can see what the agent is working on while its output scrolls by. It is only a reminder and is never sent again; press Ctrl+Up to edit and resend it.
When the agent stops working (the terminal goes idle), optionally play a sound, show a Visual Studio notification (with how long it took, plus token count for Claude Code), and run an action.
Where the prompt panel (input box and usage bars) is docked relative to the terminal.

While debugging, when the application hits an unhandled runtime exception, automatically send the exception (type, message, and stack trace) to the active code agent so it can fix it. Only sends when an agent terminal is running.
While the agent works, the status line always says "Thinking…" instead of rotating through playful words like "Pondering…" or "Noodling…". The spinner and the clock still show it is working.
